# m8/search-hint-120x36: drawn by `view::view` from a real AppState
# (crates/graft/tests/it/search_hint.rs). Not a pty capture: a character grid,
# no colour (CLAUDE.md rule 5 — colour unverified).
#
# The graph search on the corpus octopus, shipped keymap. Three frames. Right:
# running — `… matches so far …  n/N next/prev  esc cancel` (the running frame
# is the settled AppState with its search state set back to Running);
# settled — `… (1/N)  n/N next/prev  esc close`; no match — `no matches  esc close`.
# Since m8/15b the line is the header's tail and the bar is the row's keys, led by
# `n next · N prev` while the search has a hit.

## running

# m5-lane-cap-160x24.txt: 160x24, drawn by `view::view` from a real
# AppState — a scratch repository with fourteen unmerged topic
# branches forked from `main`'s base, the cursor on `main`'s tip under
# the fourteen topic tips, so fifteen columns each hold a commit in view
# (merged branches fold by default since ease-pass 06; crates/graft/tests/it/lane_cap.rs,
# capture_lane_cap_for_docs_shots, asserted). Not a pty capture: the
# terminal is ratatui's TestBackend, so this is a character grid with
# no colour attributes in it — CLAUDE.md rule 5, colour ships
# unverified.
#
# Why: the lane cap was read off the **screen's** width while the
# detail pane stood beside the graph. At 160 columns the graph gets 92
# of them and folded to twelve lanes anyway — the breakpoint for a
# width it does not have. ADR-0039's 2026-09-21 amendment, third
# instance: ask how much room this thing has, not how big the screen
# is (m5/21 item 4).
#
# What right looks like:
#  - **The two frames differ.** With the pane open the graph folds
#    more: the header says `lanes drawn: 7 of 15` and a `⋮` rail
#    stands where the folded lanes were; a topic tip whose column
#    folded draws its commit on the rail. With the pane closed the same
#    repository on the same terminal says `lanes drawn: 11 of 15`: more
#    lanes drawn. The two used to be identical, because both asked the
#    screen.
#  - Every topic tip is in view, each in a column of its own: those
#    columns are what the cap folds. A column with no commit in view is
#    not drawn at all (ease-pass 06b; the fixture reshaped for it, as
#    06f reshaped it for the fold).
#  - With the pane open the subject column starts two cells earlier
#    and every subject is still readable.
#  - Nothing reads as an error on either frame.
#
# What is **not** proven here: colour (rule 5), and whether the graph
# beside the pane reads well by eye — that is yours to judge (rule 6).
# The counts themselves are pinned by
# `lane_cap::the_pane_narrows_the_graph_so_the_graph_folds_more` and
# `view::tests::the_lane_cap_comes_from_the_graphs_room_not_the_screens_width`.
#

# m2-overview-strip.txt: TestBackend capture (not a pty), 80x24. Fixture:
# capture_m2_overview_strip in crates/graft/src/view/tests.rs (asserted;
# regenerate on purpose). Seven synthetic commits mirroring
# graft_fixtures::Shape::FeatureBranches: two feature branches each merged
# into main, main's tip (0909090) is HEAD. `strip_shown = true` (as `O`
# would set it). First block is the Unicode tier, second is ASCII
# (`F3`/`renderer_override`). The strip is bucketed over the whole 24-row
# screen (header and footer included), not just the 7 history rows, so a
# history this short only lights a handful of cells — the rest read as
# `█`/`#` (on screen) or blank (past `rows_total`).
#
# Judge by eye:
# - The graph column is one cell narrower than an ordinary capture; the
#   rightmost screen column carries the strip instead.
# - Row 0 (the header row): `●`/`*` — HEAD's row (0909090, also a merge;
#   HEAD outranks merge in the priority order).
# - Row 10: `◉`/`o` — the other merge (0404040), proportionally mapped
#   further down since 7 rows spread thin over 24 cells.
# - Rows 1-9ish: `█`/`#`, the rows currently on screen.
# - The last couple of rows before the footer: blank — past `rows_total`.
#

=== unicode ===
"                                                 7 commits  lanes drawn: 2 of 3●"
"▸ ◆▾     [HEAD] Merge branch 'topic-b'                             57y  0909090█"
"  ●      topic-b work                                              57y  0808080█"
"  ●      topic-b start                                             57y  0707070█"
"  ◉▴╮    Merge branch 'topic-a'                                    57y  0404040█"
"  ● │    topic-a work                                              57y  0303030█"
"  │ ●    topic-a start                                             57y  0202020█"
"  ◇─╯    root                                                      57y  0101010█"

# m5-hints-marked-80x24.txt: 80x24, the GraphScreen widget
# drawn into ratatui's TestBackend from a view model built by hand —
# HintContext::Marked(PlainRow { verbs: RowVerbs { take: false, amend: false } }) on a five-row corpus. Not a pty capture and
# not the app: no colour is recorded (CLAUDE.md rule 5, colour ships
# unverified), and the context is set here rather than chosen by
# `view::rows::hint_context`. The contexts a real repository can reach
# are captured through the whole app instead — m5-hints-branch-*,
# -plain-*, -uncommitted-*, -changes-*. Fixture:
# capture_hint_bar_for_docs_shots in
# crates/graft-ui/src/graph_screen/tests.rs (asserted;
# regenerate on purpose).
#
# Judge by eye: the footer's last row reads the marked row's hints for
# this width — `. explain` leads (the marker's own key), then the row's
# keys, filled from the most relevant end: each hint takes the best rung
# that still leaves room for the hints ahead of it — full, short, then
# bare key — taken per hint, never as a step the whole list takes
# together, and a hint that will not fit even at its bare key is
# dropped (ADR-0039's third amendment, 2026-09-21). The three most
# relevant never fall below their floor rung, which is their short rung
# where the user's table names one and their full verb where it does
# not, and the bar is never all hidden — never a key that does nothing.

 ◆ api  /code/api · main                         5 commits  lanes drawn: 1 of 2
  ●    Commit 5                                                    2h   0505050
▸ ◉▾   Commit 4                                                    2h   0404040
  ●    Commit 3                                                    2h   0303030
  ●▴   Commit 2                                                    2h   0202020
  ◇    Commit 1                                                    2h   0101010
